newsitem.title: UK: UK bank shares mixed after Alliance float.
newsitem.headline: UK bank shares mixed after Alliance float.

text.p: UK bank shares had a mixed reaction to the higher-than-expected opening share price of building-society-turned-bank Alliance & Leicester Plc.
The Alliance shares began trading at 542.5 pence on Monday and rose as high as 556 pence before easing to 549 pence at 0806 GMT.

"Everybody is watching Alliance & Leicester," said an analyst at one investment bank, adding that the price was considerably higher than expected . Much of the early volume was individual shareholders selling their free share entitlement through brokers.

Barclays Plc shares stood out with an 11.5 pence rise to 1021.5 pence at 0822 GMT while Abbey National shares followed with a 10 pence rise to 808.5 pence. "The Alliance has been dragging them both up for some time now," the analyst said.
But HSBC was off 3.0 pence at 1535 pence while Lloyds TSB Group Plc was flat at 532 pence and Royal Bank of Scotland was up only 0.5 pence at 530 pence.
Royal Bank's shares were weakened by a newspaper report on Sunday suggesting that its Direct Line insurance arm was likely to make a loss when the bank reports its results next month.
Analysts said the next big question for the Alliance & Leicester shares was the second auction of free shares in the company later on Monday.
"You wonder how much the market will be cajoled into bidding (for the shares)," one said.

Earlier Alliance & Leicester revealed the results of the first auction of free shares which many of the former building society's eligible savers and borrowers had decided to sell to institutional bidders via stockbroker Cazenove.
The average auction price for the more than 52 million shares sold was 522 pence per share.
